products.name: MOLECULAR SIEVES 3Ax1.5mm - 250 gm
products.short_description: High grade molecular sieves are supplied by Research Lab Fine Chem Industries. Molecular sieves are nothing but materials with holes (pores) of uniform sizes. The diameter of a molecular sieve is measured in nanometres (nm) or ngstrms (). Microporous materials have pore diameter of less than 20 (2nm) and microporous materials have a pore diameter greater than 500 (50nm). Molecular sieve is an alkali metal alumino-silicate, the potassium form of the type A crystal structure. 3A sieve is created by replacing parts of the sodium ions in the 4 sleeve with potassium ions. There are various benefits of a 3A molecular sieve include high absorption speed, higher contamination residue and extended product life. Keep the molecular sieve in an air tight container, away from moisture. CAS No. 1327-44-2 Quantity provided: 250 gm/bottle Specifications: 3A x 1.5 mm Molecular formula: 2/3K2O1/3Na2OAl2O3 2 SiO2 9/2 H2OMolecular sieves have a range of uses like static drying of insulating glass units, dehydration of highly polar compounds and dehydration of unsaturated hydrocarbons. They are also used to dry gas streams in the petroleum industry. In the laboratory, molecular sieves are used to dry solvent. Molecular sieves seem to be superior to traditional drying techniques like aggressive desiccants. They also find application in the filtration of air supplies for breathing apparatus, like the ones used by scuba divers and firefighters. The air is supplied by an air compressor and is passed through a cartridge filter which, may be filled with molecular sieve and/or activated carbon, and then used to charge breathing air tanks. Such kind of filtration can remove particulates and compressor exhaust products from the breathing air supply.

products.short_description: Morpholine is a high-grade reagent supplied by Research Lab Fine Chem Industries. Other chemical names used to denote this reagent include, 1-Oxa-4-azacyclohexane, Tetrahydro-1,4-oxazine Diethylene oxamide and Diethylenimide oxide. Because of the amine, morpholine is a base; its conjugate acid is called morpholinium. Morpholine is industrially produced by dehydration of diethanolamine with sulfuric acid. It is available in the form of a clear, colourless liquid with a characteristic amine odour (detectable over 0.1 ppm). Morpholine is soluble in water, has a boiling point of 128C and a melting point of -5C. It is stable as long it is stored as per the recommended storage conditions. Burning or prolonged exposure to heat or flammable sources can lead to the formation of hazardous decomposition products like carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxides. CAS No. 110-91-8 Quantity provided: 500 ml/bottle Molecular formula: C4H9NO Molecular weight: 87.122 g/mol Assay: Minimum 98.5%Morpholine is a common additive (in ppm) used for pH adjustment in fossil fuel and nuclear power plant steam systems. Morpholine is used because its volatility is about the same as water, so once it is added to the water, its concentration becomes distributed evenly in both the water and steam phases. Morpholine undergoes a greater number of chemical reactions than other secondary amines, though the presence of the ether oxygen withdraws electron density from the nitrogen, rendering it less nucleophilic (and less basic) than structurally similar secondary amines such as piperidine. For this reason, it forms a stable chloramine. It is commonly used to produce enamines. Morpholine is also used as a chemical emulsifier in the process of waxing fruit.

It can be used to determine cell density by staining technique. It has the ability to stain biomolecules, chromosomes and nucleic acids and is also used to stain living organisms and tissues like fungi, brain, sperms and yeast cell. products.name: BENEDICT’S REAGENT (quantitative) - 500 ml
products.short_description: Benedicts reagent by Research Lab Fine Chem Industries is a high grade reagent. This is a chemical reagent mixture of sodium carbonate, sodium citrate and copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate as well as potassium thiocyanate. It is a deep blue coloured solution. The test is based on the principle that reducing sugars when heated in the presence of an alkali, are converted to powerful reducing species known as enediols. These enediols reduce the cupric compounds present in the Benedict's reagent to cuprous compounds which are precipitated as insoluble red copper (I) oxide (Cu2O). CAS No.: 63126-89-6 Quantity Provided: 500 ml per bottle Suitable for quantitative testsBenedicts reagent has a variety of applications in chemical and biological sectors. This test for monosaccharides and reducing disaccharide sugars detects the presence of aldehydes and alpha-hydroxy-ketones, also by hemiacetal, including those that occur in certain ketoses. The quantitative test solution forms a copper thiocyanate precipitate which can be titrated to determine sugar concentration. The titration is to be repeated with 1% glucose solution instead of the sample for calibration. This reagent is suitable for industrial synthesis of products and research applications.

products.name: MOLECULAR SIEVES 4Ax1.5mm - 250 gm
products.short_description: High grade molecular sieves are supplied by Research Lab Fine Chem Industries. Molecular sieves are nothing but materials with holes (pores) of uniform sizes. The diameter of a molecular sieve is measured in nanometres (nm) or ngstrms (). Microporous materials have pore diameter of less than 20 (2nm) and microporous materials have a pore diameter greater than 500 (50nm). Molecular sieve is an alkali metal alumino-silicate, the potassium form of the type A crystal structure. These are made of sodium alumino silicate. they are used as molecular sieves in medical containers to keep contents dry. Sometimes they can also be used as food additives.Keep the molecular sieve in an air tight container, away from moisture. CAS No. 1327-39-5 Quantity provided: 250 gm/bottle Specifications: 4A x 1.5 mm Molecular formula: Na2OAl2O32SiO29/2H2OMolecular sieves have a range of uses like static drying of insulating glass units, dehydration of highly polar compounds and dehydration of unsaturated hydrocarbons. They are also used to dry gas streams in the petroleum industry. In the laboratory, molecular sieves are used to dry solvent. Molecular sieves seem to be superior to traditional drying techniques like aggressive desiccants. They also find application in the filtration of air supplies for breathing apparatus, like the ones used by scuba divers and firefighters. The air is supplied by an air compressor and is passed through a cartridge filter which, may be filled with molecular sieve and/or activated carbon, and then used to charge breathing air tanks. Such kind of filtration can remove particulates and compressor exhaust products from the breathing air supply.

The air is supplied by an air compressor and is passed through a cartridge filter which, may be filled with molecular sieve and/or activated carbon, and then used to charge breathing air tanks. Such kind of filtration can remove particulates and compressor exhaust products from the breathing air supply.

Molecular sieves seem to be superior to traditional drying techniques like aggressive desiccants. They also find application in the filtration of air supplies for breathing apparatus, like the ones used by scuba divers and firefighters. The air is supplied by an air compressor and is passed through a cartridge filter which, may be filled with molecular sieve and/or activated carbon, and then used to charge breathing air tanks. It is vastly used as the medium for analytical scale electrophoretic separation in agarose gel electrophoresis. Agarose gels have lower resolving power for DNA than acrylamide gels, but they have greater range of separation, and are therefore usually used for DNA fragments of 50-20,000 bp in size. It is also used for protein purification in chromatography.

Mica is stable when exposed to electricity, light, moisture, and extreme temperatures. It has superior electrical properties as an insulator and as a dielectric, and can support an electrostatic field while dissipating minimal energy in the form of heat; it can be split very thin (0.025 to 0.125 millimeters or thinner) while maintaining its electrical properties, has a high dielectric breakdown, is thermally stable to 500 C (932 F), and is resistant to corona discharge.
